newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Burkina president's party wins election landslide.
newsitem.headline: Burkina president's party wins election landslide.

text.p: President Blaise Compaore's ruling party won an overwhelming majority of the 111 seats in Burkina Faso's new national assembly, provisional results showed on Friday.
The results of Sunday's election in the land-locked West African nation, released by the national election commission, gave Compaore's Congress for Popular Democracy 101 seats.
The allied Alliance for Democracy and Federation of Minister of State for Integeration and African Solidarity Herman Yameogo won two seats.
Joseph Ki-Zerbo's opposition Party for Democracy and Progress won six seats, the African Democratic Rally of former prime minister Gerard Kango Ouedraogo, won two.
Compaore's party held 88 out of 107 seats in the outgoing national assembly, which was elected in 1992 during Burkina Faso's return to multi-party politics.
Parliament amended the constitution in January to increase the size of the assembly to 111.
Cash-strapped opposition parties, while hoping for victory, had said they would be content with an increased stake in the new parliament.
Compaore came to power in a 1987 army coup in which populist leader Thomas Sankara, his former close friend, was killed.
The constitution initially limited him to one seven-year term. Parliament in January voted to let him stand as many times as he wants. The next presidential election is due in 1998.
Sunday's turnout was 44.07 percent, compared to 35 percent in 1992.
